page: Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-2400s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family configured with dedicated AMD EPYC hardware. The instance delivers 24 vCPUs derived from 12 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system features 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, alongside an instruction set that includes AVX-512 extensions (AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA extensions. Memory allocation is substantial at 192.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, paired with 2400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a single complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated hardware GPUs are attached to this profile.

Benchmark assessments show solid compute execution across varied workloads. In synthetic tests, stress-ng multi-core reached 75,445.88 and PassMark CPU scored 52,038.95, both ranking in the top 25%. Geekbench single-core scored 1,892.0 while multi-core achieved 16,401.0, accompanied by strong results in text processing (2,519.0) and image processing (14,879.0). Single-core stress-ng registered in the top 10% at 3,145.78. Memory subsystems performed effectively, with the PassMark memory benchmark reaching 3,082.23 (top 10%) and uncached read-only bandwidth registering 347.13 GB/sec. Data manipulation operations such as Redis SET (58.64 million ops/sec) and PassMark database operations (12,936.09) fell into the middle 50% tier.

In language model inference benchmarks executed on CPU, the instance demonstrated strong efficiency on smaller models. Prompt processing on a 135M model reached 2,547.05 tokens per second, with generation output at 348.95 tokens per second (top 10%). On a 7B model, text generation maintained 35.13 tokens per second (top 25%), although larger 70B evaluation metrics are not available. Due to its balanced 1:8 core-to-memory ratio and bundled high-capacity NVMe drive, the instance offers strong resource density for memory-bound tasks without requiring separate external block storage overhead.

Given its high memory footprint, dedicated x86_64 cores, and local NVMe capacity, the voc-m-24c-192gb-2400s-amd is primarily suitable for in-memory databases, large-scale caching clusters, data engineering and ETL pipelines, and CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference.
